title: Globally Divergent, Locally Convergent
subtitle: The rarest and most consequential cognitive phenotype, and why it is statistically rare

blocks.text: Divergence and convergence operate at two scales, global (frame, ontology, problem space) and local (task, execution, implementation), yielding four cognitive configurations: the conventional executor, the safe innovator, the frame-divergent/task-convergent thinker, and the unbounded explorer. GDLC is the third: maximal divergence in the construction of the global frame with maximal convergence in whatever local frame has been temporarily chosen.

blocks.caption: Globally Divergent, Locally Convergent — The rarest and most consequential cognitive phenotype, and why it is statistically rare
blocks.explanation: The rarity argument is a conjunction, not a sum. Extreme global divergence and extreme local convergence impose opposite control requirements, so their co-occurrence at high levels is the product of two small probabilities under imperfect independence. The plate also separates three levels of intellectual authority — performance, mastery, and frame authorship — and notes that one can be outstanding at the first two without possessing the third.

blocks.text: Inclination is directional information over possible transitions — signed, dynamic, and central to action. It is not intent, not an act, and not execution.
